openings.claim: If rim geometry permits, paired-strip clamps with bolt-shank edge stops could carry the sideways load through bearing while modest clamp pressure retains the hatch.
openings.delta: Change the incumbent friction dependency: position outboard connecting bolts against opposing hatch edges along the pull direction, so strip assemblies anchored around the rim provide lateral stops. Drill only supplied strips. Use rubber pads at clamp contacts, alternate tightening, and tether removable assemblies and pads outside the aperture. Do not compensate for poor location by increasing corner pressure.
openings.prediction: The nearest rival is G0049:R1 with clearance around its bolts and restraint from friction alone. At comparable modest pressure, edge-stop assemblies should keep position within 1 mm under 20 N despite the final right-contact card, whereas friction-only assemblies may slide. Bearing should reduce the need for pressure that produces opposite-corner lift. These are unestablished predictions; similar performance would not distinguish the mechanisms.
openings.probe: First inspect whether bolt shanks can contact hatch edges and capture the rim within the supplied strip lengths without obstructing opening or touching the seal. Reject before fabrication if impossible. Within ninety fabrication minutes, prepare the same assemblies for two configurations. Within twenty observation minutes, give the friction-only rival two closure/pull trials, one disturbed; then give the edge-stop candidate ten numbered opening/closure/pull cycles, final closure disturbed. Record position before/after each 20 N pull, corner lift, reopening time and visible seal tears. Require final reopening within 30 seconds. Reject on damage, permanent deformation, excessive displacement or release time. Twelve trials establish only this bounded comparison.
assumptions: Rim access, bolt clearance and recoverable cord routing are indispensable unknowns; no extra parts are assumed.
Available strips and six bolts must provide stops within the 1 mm allowance without bending, slipping around the rim or permanently indenting hatch edges.
Four pads must protect clamp contacts; exposed bearing contact may make the design infeasible.
If fabrication, switching configurations or measurement exceeds the supplied time, the proposed comparison is infeasible.

assessment: A geometry-dependent probe, not deployment or demonstrated improvement. Stop contact and safe bearing capacity remain unresolved.

lineage.reason: Retain removable paired-strip clamps; add explicit bearing stops and a bounded friction rival comparison.
